reviewMethod: Complete line-by-line semantic review of the deterministic repository-audit authority, including Git-object data flow, exact-head binding, fail-closed behavior, workflow permissions, action pinning, negative-test adequacy and completion-claim boundaries.

residualRisks.statement: This bounded slice reviews nine Batch 1 audit-authority files only; test authorities remain assigned to Batch 12 and all other repository paths retain their pending status.

The workflow guard intentionally implements only the governed repository-audit YAML shape rather than the complete YAML specification; any future workflow restructuring requires policy and negative-fixture updates.

reviewNotes: Triggers, read-only permissions, exact PR-head checkout, non-persistent credentials, expected-SHA propagation, authority verification, manifest regeneration, tests and immutable artifact upload were reviewed as one fail-closed sequence.
All third-party actions are pinned to full commit SHAs and the artifact name is bound to the exact reviewed head.
All scripts, dependency pins, engine constraints and override declarations were reviewed; the audit commands remain exact and separated between generation, authority checking, verification and tests.

The added ESLint, secret-scanning and operational-recovery commands bind their permanent guards to focused tests, while env:check now composes the existing environment validator with the production CSP connection validator.
The release path uses npm ci and governed checks; mutable developer convenience commands remain outside release authority.

findings.attackPath: A developer invoking install:safe or ci:safe transitively runs npm:registry:fix, which changes persistent npm registry configuration and removes proxy settings outside the repository.
findings.affectedInvariant: Repository convenience commands should not silently mutate persistent host package-manager configuration.
findings.evidence: package.json lines 104 and 107-108 use npm config set/delete before repository-scoped install commands.
findings.verificationRequirement: Replace persistent npm config mutation with command-scoped registry/proxy inputs or an explicit opt-in repair command, then prove normal ci:safe execution leaves user npm configuration unchanged.

reviewNotes: Filesystem scope, ignored runtime outputs, import extraction, local resolution, entrypoint reachability, artifact heuristics, dependency ownership, bounded reporting and non-deletion warning were reviewed line by line.
Package-binary ownership now preserves the regular-expression whitespace class at runtime instead of collapsing it inside a JavaScript template literal.

findings.attackPath: A package binary referenced after whitespace in package scripts was not recognized because the template literal consumed the regex backslash, producing a false unreferenced-dependency lead.
findings.affectedInvariant: Repository hygiene evidence must not classify an owned dependency as unreferenced because of a malformed scanner boundary.
findings.evidence: The former template literal used [\s;&|] in source semantics that evaluated as [s;&|]; the final source escapes the backslash and the authority guard preserves that contract.
findings.verificationRequirement: The permanent authority check must reject removal of the escaped whitespace boundary and the hygiene report must continue to execute successfully.

reviewNotes: The guard verifies workflow authority, committed evidence schema/batch identity, runtime-artifact hygiene exclusion, both package-binary whitespace boundaries and exact package command ownership before manifest generation.

findings.attackPath: A later scanner edit could regress only the leading package-binary whitespace class while leaving the trailing class intact, allowing the former single-substring guard to pass and miss package binaries after shell separators.
findings.affectedInvariant: Repository hygiene evidence must preserve both package-binary boundary classes so dependency ownership is not undercounted.
findings.evidence: The former authority check required only one escaped boundary occurrence; the remediated guard counts the source occurrences and requires at least two.
findings.verificationRequirement: The permanent authority check must fail if either escaped package-binary whitespace boundary is removed.

reviewNotes: Output resolution, parent creation, truncating write semantics and summary logging were reviewed; generated runtime evidence remains outside the tracked denominator.

Git subprocess environment, byte-level NUL parsing, UTF-8 fail-closed decoding, blob batching, gitlink handling, deterministic sorting, digest/line accounting and bounded automated scanning were reviewed line by line.

Semantic declarations are read from the exact Git blob set, require sorted unique paths, exact blob/digest/line identity, contiguous full-line coverage, structured findings and exact-head reviewedCommitSha binding.
Canonical finding identifiers now bind their embedded P0-P3 priority to the structured severity field before evidence can be applied.
Every evidence declaration configured by Policy v9 must exist in the exact tracked tree; generation and verification reject a committed deletion instead of silently emitting an empty evidence set.
Summary recomputation occurs after evidence application and completionClaim remains false.

findings.attackPath: A declaration could encode P0 in its canonical finding identifier while separately declaring P3, presenting contradictory release severity to downstream consumers.
findings.affectedInvariant: A canonical finding identifier and its structured severity must represent one unambiguous priority.
findings.evidence: The former validator checked the ID shape and severity membership independently but did not compare the ID priority segment with finding.severity.
findings.verificationRequirement: Manifest generation must reject a B01A-P0 identifier paired with P3 severity before semantic evidence is applied.

findings.attackPath: Deleting a configured evidence declaration while leaving its policy entry intact could previously produce a schema-valid manifest with an empty reviewEvidenceSets array.
findings.affectedInvariant: Every semantic evidence path configured by the audit policy must exist in the exact tracked tree before generation or verification can succeed.
findings.evidence: The former loop continued when filesByPath did not contain a configured declaration, silently downgrading previously recorded semantic review evidence.
findings.verificationRequirement: A committed deletion of batch-01a-audit-authority.json must make both manifest generation and verification fail closed.

reviewNotes: Generated/vendored ownership, explicit repository-supply-chain authorities, ordered domain rules, source-path fail-closed behavior, provenance-driven pending state, twelve batches and Policy v9 evidence-path ownership were reviewed.
Tests/docs precedence is intentional for Batch 12; operations precedes repository-supply classification for runtime authorities.

Comment handling, scalar parsing, indentation and block boundaries, exact governed step sequence, permissions, exact-head propagation, reserved variable rejection, full-SHA action pinning and aggregate failure reporting were reviewed.
Required executable contracts are now validated at their effective governed YAML nodes with exact keys and values instead of arbitrary substring presence.

findings.attackPath: A required checkout, verification or artifact contract could be removed from executable YAML and preserved only as a comment while the former substring guard still returned success.
findings.affectedInvariant: Repository audit evidence must fail closed when an exact-head workflow control is not executable.
findings.evidence: The previous guard used unrestricted includes() checks; the final implementation parses the governed YAML structure and validates exact effective step nodes, keys, values and sequence.
findings.verificationRequirement: Negative fixtures must move each governed contract into a comment and observe a policy failure; the unchanged real workflow must pass.

reviewNotes: Input resolution, strict JSON parsing, full regeneration/structural comparison and verified-denominator reporting were reviewed; malformed or stale artifacts fail before success output.
